summary: SE-led troubleshooting session to correlate HorizonCore's observed latency spikes with Redwood request traces, KV cache behavior and fallback to smaller model variants. Identified candidate root causes: inconsistent prefix caching, intermittent KV cache cold starts, and a small subset of long-context prompts that bypass batching. Agreed next steps: share traces and pilot proposal.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, this is Priya our solutions engineer. How's the morning over there?
[00:08] Olivia Marquez: Morning, hey Jordan, thanks. We've got Marta and Dinesh on to walk through the traces you asked for.
[00:15] Priya Nair: Great, thanks Olivia. We'll start by recapping the incidents you sent 11/23 — high tail latency for chat endpoints, then walk through how to use the Console trace playback and correlate with request logs.
[00:28] Marta Cole: Yup, so we saw a couple spikes where p95 goes to 2.1s and p99 hits around 3.8s on a few user journeys. They looked like they were coming from a particular customer segment but we weren't able to map request ids to any obvious infra events.
[00:42] Dinesh Rao: And to add, we had a short window where our autoscaler kicked in new dedicated pods, but not sure if that lines up.
[00:50] Priya Nair: Okay great. If you pasted the request ids in the ticket those are what we used to pull traces. I'll share the console links in chat after the call. Note: console links are time-limited.
[01:05] Jordan Lee: Quick housekeeping — we'll record action items at the end. Also, a reminder that some of the labels in the auto-transcript are fuzzy; ignore any garbled product names.
[01:13] Marta Cole: ha yeah the transcriber always makes 'KV cache' into 'K V case' which is fine.
[01:18] Priya Nair: Alright jumping in — opening the first trace. This one is request id rc-7112. You can see the waterfall: request queue -> prefix cache check -> model dispatch. I'm seeing a KV cache miss followed by a synchronous fetch to the cold store at ~120ms which added about 90ms to token generation on the initial request.
[01:36] Dinesh Rao: That synchronous fetch, is that on our side or Redwood's managed cache?
[01:40] Priya Nair: It's our managed prefix/KV cache layer that we run in the serving path. Typically it's async-prefetch for longer prefixes but for some first-request patterns it can be sync. We have a config that toggles keep-warm prefetch but you need to tune it per workload.
[01:54] Olivia Marquez: We don't currently pin prefixes; our traffic is pretty spiky with new users so cold prefixes are common.
[02:01] Priya Nair: Makes sense, that will increase cold starts. Also looking at the same trace there's a model fallback path where the router decided to fall back to a smaller quantized variant after a 400ms queue because of slot contention. That fallback added another 150-200ms.
[02:18] Marta Cole: So we had both a KV miss and a fallback in the same request? That's kinda brutal.
[02:22] Priya Nair: Yeah, compounded effects. The console trace shows the decisions: routing policy eval -> capacity check -> fallback to variant-a-q4. You can toggle the 'show decision' checkbox to see policy reasons.
[02:35] Jordan Lee: Quick commercial aside — if you want deterministic capacity we can reserve a dedicated pool; avoids fallbacks but there's a commit. We'll talk pricing later.
[02:44] Olivia Marquez: We might be open to a small reserved buffer if it fixes p99. Need to see numbers.
[02:50] Priya Nair: Totally. Back to the trace — I'm also seeing batching behavior. For most requests we batch by short time windows, but a handful of requests with long prompts prevented effective batching. Those long-context prompts serialized execution which amplifies tail latency.
[03:07] Dinesh Rao: Those prompts were from one integration partner — we can throttle on our side but would prefer Redwood recommendations.
[03:14] Priya Nair: We usually recommend: 1) prefix-truncation for non-essential context; 2) enable conservative batching window for chat flows; 3) increase prefetch / keep-warm for hot prefixes. We can provide a config snippet.
[03:28] Marta Cole: Can the console show the exact prompt length and token counts?
[03:31] Priya Nair: Yes there's a token breakdown in the payload view. Sometimes the transcribed token counts in the UI are off by one due to tokenizer differences, but it's close.
[03:40] [05:00] Jordan Lee: (background) okay jumping ahead — question from Dinesh?
[05:05] Dinesh Rao: Sorry I just wanted to confirm: when a fallback happens, do we get an event/log we can query? We need to tie it back to our monitoring.
[05:12] Priya Nair: Yes, the console emits an event and it's also present in the request logs as 'router.fallback.reason' with reason codes like 'capacity' or 'cost-tier'. You can export those logs to your SIEM (we've seen Datadog and Splunk used frequently).
[05:25] Dinesh Rao: Great — and those logs contain the AVAIL pool id?
[05:29] Priya Nair: Pool id and model variant id yes, and the region tag.
[05:33] Marta Cole: We noticed also some misattributed latency spikes where the trace shows a 500ms network delay between our proxy and the Redwood edge, but our infra metrics didn't show packet loss. Could it be transient congestion?
[05:50] Priya Nair: Could be. The console provides a timeline that includes client RTT and server-side processing. If client RTT is elevated but backend looks fine that's often a network hop issue. We also surface gzipped payload sizes — in one incident we saw a very large prompt with attachments which changed compression behavior.
[06:07] Olivia Marquez: Attachments, right — some of our users paste base64 images and that kills tokenization — good to know.
[06:12] Priya Nair: Yep. Next, I'll show the trace playback feature — when you click the timestamped event it highlights the corresponding log lines and any recorded kernel-level latencies.
[06:24] [08:00] Priya Nair: (screen) Here you can see the KV cache TTLs; one of the prefixes had TTL set to 30s due to our default. When traffic is spiky, that TTL causes frequent cold fetches. We can suggest bumping to 5m for high-value prefixes.
[08:37] Marta Cole: Is there a slot for a keep-warm job in Redwood or we do that client-side?
[08:42] Priya Nair: We can enable an internal keep-warm prefetch for pinned prefixes as part of the dedicated offering, or you can client-side call a warming endpoint during off-peak. Both work.
[08:53] Dinesh Rao: About the model variants — you mentioned routing policy, can that be policy-by-API-key? We want some partners to hit higher-cost models.
[09:01] Priya Nair: Yes, routing policies can be keyed by API key, route, or customer metadata. We can do per-tenant cost tiers so partner traffic can be prioritized to the full-precision model.
[09:12] Jordan Lee: Allright quick pause — Olivia, is security/compliance a blocker for pushing pilot to prod?
[09:17] Olivia Marquez: We need SOC 2 and KMS integration. We have a compliance review next week.
[09:22] Jordan Lee: We have SOC 2 Type II, plus KMS integrations with AWS KMS and options for customer-managed keys in Private deployments. I'll attach the security pack after this call.
[09:32] Marta Cole: Please include audit log retention options — we need 1 year by default.
[09:36] Jordan Lee: Noted.
[09:38] [12:00] Priya Nair: Back to traces — I'm pulling up a couple of high p99s. Trace rc-7128 shows a rare codepath where a large system prompt forced full attention over the sequence and the runtime switched kernels which caused a spike during kernel selection. Kernel switching can be a few hundred milliseconds. We can precompile kernels for your common sequence lengths.
[12:25] Dinesh Rao: That sounds like an optimization we should do. Is that part of Redwood Optimize?
[12:29] Priya Nair: Exactly — Optimize suggests kernel profiles and quantization for workloads. For pilot we'll run a quick profiler across sample traffic.
[12:37] Marta Cole: Any risk of quality regression if we bump quant?
[12:40] Priya Nair: We run evals on your prompt set and we can surface BLEU/ROUGE-style regressions and false-positive tests. We also do A/B rollouts with automatic fallback to baseline if quality drops.
[12:51] [15:00] Olivia Marquez: A couple of practical questions — how do we get a persistent link for a trace to save in our incident tracker?
[15:07] Priya Nair: Links are time-limited by default but we can create a permalink export that pushes the trace bundle (anonymized) to an S3 bucket you control — good for CTI. We'll put that in the security doc.
[15:19] Marta Cole: For our monitoring we want a daily digest of fallback reasons and top failing routes. Can Redwood send that?
[15:25] Jordan Lee: Yes we can ship a daily webhook or an S3 CSV. We'll include a sample schema.
[15:31] Dinesh Rao: On the billing side, if we reserve capacity but still occasionally burst beyond it, what's the fallback?
[15:37] Jordan Lee: Burst goes to public/shared pools if configured; you can choose strict-siloed reserved-only behavior which will reject excess requests. There's also automatic prioritized bursting for enterprise tiers.
[15:45] Olivia Marquez: We'd prefer prioritized bursting with alerting on exceeded commit.
[15:49] Jordan Lee: We can set a budget alert and send to Slack or PagerDuty.
[15:53] [20:00] Priya Nair: Quick demo of request-log search: you can filter by model, region, fallback.reason and token_count. Use the 'correlate with trace' checkbox to jump directly from a log row into console playback.
[20:15] Marta Cole: Nice. That'll speed up our incident turnaround time.
[20:21] Dinesh Rao: We also want to be sure logs include correlated span ids for our distributed tracing; do you emit a tracing/span id that maps to our existing X-Trace header?
[20:30] Priya Nair: We do. We surface both Redwood trace id and honor customer-supplied trace headers (X-B3, W3C). The console will link them for you.
[20:39] Olivia Marquez: Any concern about PII in traces? We need guidance on redaction and retention.
[20:45] Priya Nair: We support automatic redaction rules and can redact prompt text or store only hashes. Retention policies configurable per workspace. We'll include the redaction playbook in the docs.
[20:58] [25:00] Jordan Lee: Let's talk about pilot success metrics: target p99 under 1.2s for chat; reduce fallback rate under 0.5% and keep token cost within 10% of current. Does that sound reasonable?
[25:12] Olivia Marquez: Sounds good but need to confirm with finance — p99 target is the big one.
[25:18] Marta Cole: Also SLO for error rate below 0.05%.
[25:21] Jordan Lee: We'll bake that into the pilot SLA.
[25:24] [28:00] Priya Nair: Closing out with the deep-dive checklist — I'll attach: 1) trace snippets (done), 2) config recommendations (keep-warm, TTLs, batching windows), 3) sample pilot script (load levels and verification prompts), 4) security pack (KMS/SOC2/audit retention).
[28:43] Dinesh Rao: One nit — the console token counter shows 1 token off sometimes; we've seen that when people use emoji in prompts. Not a blocker but FYI.
[28:52] Priya Nair: Yep tokenizer nuance, we annotate that in Optimize results.
[28:56] Olivia Marquez: Can we get a short runbook for incident triage using the console?
[29:01] Priya Nair: Absolutely, we'll share a 1-pager with the top 8 steps: locate trace by id -> expand decision tree -> check KV cache TTLs -> check fallback.reason -> check kernel switch events -> correlate client RTT -> export permalink -> open ticket.
[29:18] Jordan Lee: Perfect. Any final questions?
[29:21] Marta Cole: Not for now. We'll wait for the trace bundles and pilot proposal.
[29:26] Dinesh Rao: One last: can we run a short synthetic load test against a dev model to validate batching improvements?
[29:31] Priya Nair: Yes we can run a controlled benchmark. We'll need a traffic sample and preferred SLA window.
[29:38] Jordan Lee: Okay wrapping up — I'll send the security pack and pilot pricing. Priya will send the trace artifacts. Marta you'll share the incident ids.
[29:48] Olivia Marquez: Thanks everyone.
[29:50] Jordan Lee: Thanks, talk soon.
[29:53] [End of recording — approximate timestamps for long sections omitted in transcript]

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mis-heard tokens (K V case), product names sometimes munged, timestamps approximate. Links shared in chat (not included): console.trace/rc-7112, console.trace/rc-7128, s3://horizoncore-redwood/traces/20261130_bundle.zip

Recap / Decisions:
- Root causes identified: KV cache cold starts, model-variant fallback due to capacity, and long-context prompts reducing batching efficiency.
- Temporary mitigations: bump TTL for hot prefixes, enable client-side warming, throttle partner long prompts.
- Longer-term: pilot with small dedicated pool and Optimize profiling to precompile kernels and tune quantization.

End of export.
